Calculate union-years, dissolutions and duration-specific rates

Source: R/calculate_dissolution_rates.R
calculate_dissolution_rates.Rd

Split each union episode across calendar periods and elapsed-duration bands, counting union-years once per episode, not once per spouse. Death and dissolution both stop exposure, but only end_reason = "dissolution" counts toward dissolutions. Missing ends are censored at the observation endpoint. Repeated episodes are separate observations; distinct overlapping records are not merged. Analyze one independent history per call, then combine counts.

Usage

calculate_dissolution_rates(
  population,
  time_breaks,
  dur_breaks,
  by_group = FALSE,
  by_union_type = FALSE,
  conf.level = NULL
)

Arguments

population

A hammel_population, or a union data frame containing unique positive whole-number union_id, start_time, end_time, and end_reason. Ends and reasons are NA for ongoing episodes; ended reasons are "dissolution", "death_husband", "death_wife", or "conversion". Population objects need a known endpoint; observation cannot extend beyond it. For bare tables, ensure complete follow-up through the requested endpoint.

time_breaks

Strictly increasing finite calendar boundaries in years.

dur_breaks

Strictly increasing nonnegative duration boundaries in years. If the last boundary is finite, append Inf for an open final band.

by_group

Logical, default FALSE. With TRUE, use unordered group pairs and return group_pair (e.g. "A:A", "A:B", "B:B"). Both directions of a cross-group union share one stratum. Population inputs require person groups and retain every unordered pair in the full period/duration grid. Bare union tables require group_pair; reversed labels are normalized. Pair labels use nonempty colon-free character representations of groups, ordered alphabetically (radix). Empty grouped inputs return a typed zero-row tibble; no pooled row is added.

by_union_type

Logical, default FALSE. Separate cohabitation and marriage episodes using each type's own exposure. Requires a valid union_type column. Conversion stops cohabitation exposure without counting as dissolution; duration resets at the start of the linked marriage episode.

conf.level

NULL (default) to omit confidence intervals, or a finite numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. Adds conf_low and conf_high from two-sided exact stats::poisson.test() intervals for observed event counts over exposure. Bounds are NA at zero exposure. For fertility, these describe the observed rate, not the unrealized-adjusted rate.

Value

A tibble with time_start, time_end, dur_start, dur_end, union_years, dissolutions, and rate_dissolution, plus group_pair and union_type when requested. Period varies fastest within duration bands and group blocks. With non-NULL conf.level, also includes conf_low and conf_high.

Details

Exposure and event cells are half-open. Dissolutions at internal boundaries belong to the cell beginning there, and events at the last time boundary are excluded. Zero-duration episodes may contribute events with no exposure. Rates are dissolutions per union-year: zero with positive exposure and no events, and NA when exposure is zero. This is a cause-specific rate, not the probability of dissolution in the presence of competing partner deaths.

Examples

unions <- data.frame(union_id = 1:3, start_time = c(0, 1, 2),
  end_time = c(3, 4, NA),
  end_reason = c("dissolution", "death_husband", NA))
calculate_dissolution_rates(unions, c(0, 2, 5), c(0, 2, Inf))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   time_start time_end dur_start dur_end union_years dissolutions
#>        <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1          0        2         0       2           3            0
#> 2          2        5         0       2           3            0
#> 3          0        2         2     Inf           0            0
#> 4          2        5         2     Inf           3            1
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: rate_dissolution <dbl>
